methodology: Separate online signals available during one interaction, nearline signals available after short aggregation, and offline signals requiring longitudinal or external evidence.
Treat signals as review leads, not findings. Every risk includes a plausible authorized-use twin and a false-positive path.
Prefer public primary guidance from standards bodies, government agencies, protocol publishers, and service providers. Avoid operational detail that would enable abuse.

timing_definitions.online: Available in the current request, response, tool call, session state, or authenticated runtime context and fast enough to inform a bounded real-time decision.
timing_definitions.nearline: Available after minutes to hours of aggregation, enrichment, sandboxing, or cross-session comparison; it may inform containment or queued review but not the already completed interaction.
timing_definitions.offline: Available through days-to-months longitudinal analysis, case investigation, external reports, evaluation, or adjudication.

risks.name: Cyber abuse
risks.harm: Model or agent use may support unauthorized access, malware activity, vulnerability exploitation, or disruptive operations.

online: Requests combine exploit intent with live-target context, credential material, or execution-capable tool calls.
Tool results show unexpected privilege changes, outbound connections, or writes outside an authorized test boundary.
nearline: A short-window sequence progresses from reconnaissance to exploit adaptation to persistence across sessions or tools.
Repeated attempts target many unrelated hosts or bypass earlier safeguards.
offline: Case correlation links activity to confirmed incidents, abuse reports, malware telemetry, or violated authorization boundaries.
Longitudinal review finds coordinated infrastructure or recurring exploit chains.

authorized_use_twins: A documented penetration test, capture-the-flag exercise, defensive reverse engineering, vulnerability reproduction, or incident-response investigation can produce the same technical vocabulary and tool sequence.
false_positive_factors: Code snippets and security terms do not establish malicious intent; scope, ownership, authorization, target, and execution context matter.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Security-abuse analyst trained to distinguish defensive testing from unauthorized operations
reviewer_path.escalation_role: Incident-response lead or product security owner with authority over the affected boundary
evidence_requirements: Preserve the request/tool/result sequence, actor and tenant context, target indicators, stated authorization, detector version, and contradictory evidence.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: A separate reviewer rechecks scope and authorization; restoration or continued restriction records reasons and corrective evidence.

limitations: Intent is rarely observable from one prompt, and sensitive incident context may be unavailable to the analyzer.
unresolved_questions: How can organizations attest test authorization without exposing sensitive network scope to an external analyzer?

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
sources.claim_supported: Security analysis needs explicit attack life-cycle, capability, knowledge, and objective distinctions rather than a keyword-only label.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK
sources.claim_supported: Cyber behavior can be organized as tactics and techniques across an observed sequence, supporting staged rather than single-event review.

risks.name: Chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear misuse
risks.harm: Assistance could lower barriers to harmful acquisition, design, production, or deployment involving CBRN materials.

online: The interaction seeks harmful optimization, scale, acquisition, concealment, or deployment and combines it with operational context.
Tool calls attempt to source restricted materials or validate hazardous procedures.
nearline: Multiple individually ambiguous questions compose into an end-to-end harmful workflow.
The actor repeatedly reformulates requests to overcome safety boundaries or obtain missing operational steps.
offline: Qualified subject-matter review assesses whether the sequence materially increases harmful capability beyond public high-level knowledge.
External threat intelligence or lawful reports provide context unavailable in the interaction.

authorized_use_twins: Biosafety, emergency response, nonproliferation, public-health, academic, and industrial safety work can use the same entities and process terminology.
false_positive_factors: Technical specificity can reflect legitimate expertise; classification requires purpose, capability uplift, safeguards, and authorization, not topic alone.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Specialist safety reviewer operating from minimized and compartmented evidence
reviewer_path.escalation_role: Qualified CBRN subject-matter expert plus accountable safety authority
evidence_requirements: Preserve the minimum necessary sequence, model outputs, tool actions, capability-uplift rationale, authorized context, and uncertainty without redistributing hazardous detail.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: Independent specialist review checks lawful research or safety context and can narrow, reverse, or sustain the decision with a recorded basis.

limitations: General reviewers and language models can misjudge feasibility; handling detailed evidence can itself create safety and privacy risk.
unresolved_questions: What redacted evidence is sufficient for accountable appeal without spreading sensitive operational information?

sources.title: Preparedness Framework
sources.claim_supported: The framework treats biological/chemical capability as a tracked severe-harm category and uses safeguards reports and review rather than topic matching alone.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy
sources.claim_supported: Anthropic separates capability thresholds, evaluations, safeguards, and governance for catastrophic biological and chemical risks.

risks.name: Fraud and deception
risks.harm: Generated content or agent actions may facilitate impersonation, payment diversion, identity theft, scams, or deceptive transactions.

online: Requests combine impersonation, urgency, secrecy, payment routing, identity artifacts, or evasion of verification.
Agent actions alter payee, recovery, identity, or messaging fields without expected authorization evidence.
nearline: Templates or messages are sent at volume to unrelated recipients, or payment/recovery details change repeatedly.
A cluster shares scripts, infrastructure, beneficiary details, or synthetic identities.
offline: Chargebacks, victim reports, verified impersonation, account investigations, or lawfully shared fraud intelligence corroborate harm.
Longitudinal analysis links campaigns, mule accounts, or repeated social-engineering patterns.

authorized_use_twins: Fraud simulation, brand-protection exercises, customer-support drafting, debt collection under policy, and authorized marketing can include urgency, financial terms, and message templates.
false_positive_factors: A payment request or persuasive tone alone is weak evidence; recipient consent, sender identity, transaction authority, and campaign context are needed.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Fraud operations analyst with access to transaction and identity context under least privilege
evidence_requirements: Preserve content provenance, actor/account history, recipient and transaction context, authentication events, model/tool actions, and counterevidence.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: A reviewer independent of the initial decision examines identity and transaction evidence and records remediation, restriction, or reinstatement.

limitations: False reports, compromised reporters, delayed payment evidence, and privacy constraints can make adjudication incomplete.
unresolved_questions: How should cross-service campaign evidence be shared without creating a new identity or financial surveillance dataset?

sources.title: Impersonator scams: What you need to know
sources.claim_supported: Impersonation scams commonly use unexpected contact, urgency, and payment demands, but the guidance relies on context rather than any single phrase.

sources.title: Business Email Compromise
sources.claim_supported: Business email compromise includes impersonation and fraudulent transfer requests, often involving account compromise or spoofing.

risks.name: Compromised accounts
risks.harm: An unauthorized actor may use a legitimate account, credentials, API key, or session to access data, invoke tools, or conceal other abuse.

online: Authentication risk changes abruptly, impossible or unusual travel appears, or a sensitive action lacks expected step-up verification.
Session behavior diverges sharply from the account's recent device, network, model, tool, or data-access pattern.
nearline: Concurrent sessions, recovery changes, token creation, privilege changes, or rapid data access form an anomalous sequence.
A credential or infrastructure indicator appears across several accounts.
offline: User reports, forensic review, identity-provider logs, secret-scanning findings, or incident evidence confirm or refute unauthorized use.
Post-incident analysis identifies the compromise window and affected actions.

authorized_use_twins: Travel, VPN changes, new devices, automation, incident-response access, shared enterprise egress, and role changes can resemble account takeover.
false_positive_factors: Behavioral baselines can encode accessibility, geography, work pattern, or organizational bias and should not establish compromise alone.

reviewer_path.escalation_role: Security incident responder or tenant security administrator
evidence_requirements: Preserve authentication/session events, credential lifecycle, sensitive actions, notification attempts, user response, and the detector baseline used.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: The verified account owner or tenant administrator can challenge the finding through a recovery channel separate from the suspected session.

limitations: Attackers may inherit normal devices or sessions, while legitimate users may have highly variable behavior.
unresolved_questions: How much behavioral history is proportionate to retain for appeal and forensic review?

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management
sources.claim_supported: Authentication assurance, session management, phishing resistance, recovery, and notification are distinct controls relevant to suspected compromise.

sources.title: Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA
sources.claim_supported: Phishing-resistant MFA reduces credential-phishing risk, supporting step-up and recovery controls rather than behavioral inference alone.

risks.name: Model extraction
risks.harm: Systematic querying or artifact access may reconstruct model behavior, parameters, proprietary prompts, or other protected implementation details.

online: A request probes boundaries, confidence, logits, hidden prompts, or highly structured input spaces beyond the normal product contract.
Tool actions attempt unauthorized model-file, weight, checkpoint, or serving-artifact access.
nearline: High-volume adaptive queries cover a broad input space, repeat near decision boundaries, or coordinate across accounts.
Query patterns optimize information gain while varying identities or rate-limit domains.
offline: Longitudinal analysis estimates extraction coverage and links accounts, infrastructure, copied artifacts, or a demonstrably similar surrogate.
Forensics confirm unauthorized artifact access or exfiltration.

authorized_use_twins: Authorized red-team evaluation, interoperability testing, model benchmarking, distillation under license, research reproducibility, and regression testing can produce systematic query grids.
false_positive_factors: Volume and repeated templates can reflect legitimate batch workloads; rights, product terms, research approval, and information-gain pattern matter.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Abuse analyst with model-serving and customer-contract context
reviewer_path.escalation_role: Model security owner and accountable legal or product authority
evidence_requirements: Preserve query sequence features, account linkage basis, rate-limit context, artifact access logs, authorization or license terms, and similarity methodology.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: An independent reviewer verifies workload authorization and methodology before sustaining restrictions or restoring access.

limitations: Similarity does not prove extraction, and aggressive monitoring can penalize accessibility tools, researchers, or high-volume customers.
unresolved_questions: Which extraction indicators remain meaningful when outputs are sampled and normal batch usage is highly diverse?

sources.title: Exfiltration via ML Inference API
sources.claim_supported: MITRE ATLAS documents repeated inference queries as one route to infer model information and lists monitoring and rate controls as mitigations.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
sources.claim_supported: NIST distinguishes model extraction and privacy attacks by attacker knowledge, capability, objective, and life-cycle stage.

risks.name: Evasion and obfuscation
risks.harm: An actor may transform inputs, identities, or interaction sequences to avoid classifiers, policy checks, rate controls, or reviewer understanding.

online: Input contains unusual encodings, homoglyphs, fragmentation, indirection, or instruction patterns that conflict with the stated benign task.
The actor immediately retries a blocked request with semantic-preserving transformations.
nearline: Repeated paraphrases, language shifts, account changes, or staged partial requests converge on the same restricted outcome.
Different actors reuse a transformation template against the same control.
offline: Evaluation against held-out transformations shows systematic detector blind spots.
Campaign review links successful bypasses to prior failed attempts and shared infrastructure.

authorized_use_twins: Internationalization, accessibility, privacy-preserving text, data-cleaning, robustness testing, adversarial evaluation, and ordinary editing can produce unusual encoding or repeated paraphrases.
false_positive_factors: Obfuscation-like form is not intent; meaning, outcome, prior decisions, accessibility, language, and authorized red-team context must be reviewed.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Trust-and-safety analyst with multilingual and accessibility escalation paths
evidence_requirements: Preserve original and normalized forms, transformation steps, prior related requests, model/control versions, language context, and authorized test records.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: A reviewer evaluates the unnormalized original and accessibility/language context, not only the detector's normalized representation.

limitations: Normalization can destroy evidence, change meaning, or disproportionately harm multilingual and disabled users.
unresolved_questions: How should raw and normalized representations be retained and displayed without creating unsafe rendering paths?

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
sources.claim_supported: NIST defines evasion attacks and organizes them by stage, attacker goals, knowledge, capabilities, and mitigations.

risks.name: Prompt injection
risks.harm: Untrusted instructions in user or retrieved content may redirect an agent, disclose protected context, misuse tools, or override the application's intended control flow.

online: Untrusted content contains instructions aimed at the model or tool layer and conflicts with the trusted task.
A tool request crosses the expected capability, data, recipient, or confirmation boundary after processing external content.
nearline: Several retrieved items or messages compose into a hidden instruction chain followed by anomalous tool behavior.
A source, template, or payload repeatedly triggers similar control-flow divergence.
offline: Replay in a sandbox reproduces the instruction-to-action path across pinned model, prompt, tool, and policy versions.
Incident analysis identifies data exposure or unauthorized action and the trust boundary that failed.

authorized_use_twins: Security testing, prompt-injection evaluations, documents that discuss instructions, code examples, quoted conversations, and agent-development fixtures can contain the same phrases.
false_positive_factors: Instruction-like text is common in legitimate documents; provenance, trust level, control-flow effect, tool authorization, and actual outcome are required.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Application security reviewer with agent/tool context
reviewer_path.escalation_role: Product security owner and affected data or tool owner
evidence_requirements: Preserve trusted instructions, untrusted content provenance, retrieved context, model/tool calls, authorization decisions, outputs, and version digests.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: A separate reviewer replays a minimized case in a sandbox and distinguishes quoted or evaluative content from effective control-flow manipulation.

limitations: Prompt injection cannot be solved by a classifier alone; tool least privilege, isolation, confirmation, and output handling remain necessary.
unresolved_questions: Which replay representation is safe and deterministic enough for appeals when models and external content change?

sources.title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
sources.claim_supported: Prompt injection may be direct or indirect and requires layered mitigations including constrained behavior, least privilege, trust boundaries, and human approval for high-risk actions.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
sources.claim_supported: NIST's adversarial ML taxonomy includes prompt injection and distinguishes attack stages and capabilities.

risks.name: Insider risk
risks.harm: A trusted user, contractor, administrator, or service identity may misuse legitimate access, intentionally or accidentally, causing disclosure, fraud, sabotage, or policy bypass.

online: A privileged action exceeds the current role, ticket, change window, data purpose, or separation-of-duties requirement.
An agent attempts sensitive export or policy change without required confirmation or dual control.
nearline: Access volume, destination, timing, privilege changes, or denied retries diverge from current duties and approved workflows.
Multiple weak indicators align across identity, endpoint, repository, and data systems.
offline: A multidisciplinary investigation correlates access logs with approvals, role history, endpoint evidence, interviews, and actual impact.
Periodic access review identifies accumulated privilege, dormant accounts, or control gaps.

authorized_use_twins: On-call response, migrations, audits, data-science work, e-discovery, support, role transitions, and emergency administration may produce unusual privileged access.
false_positive_factors: Workforce monitoring can be intrusive and biased; unusual behavior alone must not be treated as malicious intent or an employment conclusion.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Least-privileged security analyst operating under documented insider-risk governance
reviewer_path.escalation_role: Multidisciplinary insider-risk lead with security, privacy, legal, human-resources, and business representation as applicable
evidence_requirements: Preserve access and approval records, current job duties, change/incident context, detector rationale, exculpatory evidence, and access audit history.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: A documented employee or contractor review process separates technical containment from personnel adjudication and permits correction of role or context errors.

limitations: Monitoring itself can harm privacy, labor rights, psychological safety, and due process; access and retention must be tightly governed.
unresolved_questions: Which signals are proportionate and lawful across jurisdictions and employment arrangements?

sources.title: Insider Threat Mitigation Guide
sources.claim_supported: CISA recommends a multidisciplinary, risk-based insider-threat program with defined stakeholders and privacy, civil-rights, and civil-liberties considerations.

risks.name: Coordinated actors
risks.harm: Multiple accounts, services, agents, or operators may coordinate to scale abuse, evade per-account controls, manipulate discourse, or divide a harmful workflow.

online: The current interaction shares a high-confidence infrastructure, artifact, beneficiary, or campaign identifier with an active reviewed case.
Several agents divide sequential tasks while passing distinctive state or outputs between them.
nearline: Accounts synchronize content, timing, targets, tools, or recovery/payment details beyond plausible coincidence.
A campaign rotates accounts after controls while preserving scripts, infrastructure, or objectives.
offline: Graph analysis and human investigation establish coordination using multiple independent indicators and external context.
Longitudinal review distinguishes a campaign from organic similarity, shared news, common software, or authorized teamwork.

authorized_use_twins: Teams, classrooms, incident responders, open-source communities, marketing campaigns, load tests, and shared enterprise infrastructure naturally synchronize actions and content.
false_positive_factors: Shared language, IP addresses, time zones, clients, or popular links are weak and can encode geography, organization, or community membership.

reviewer_path.triage_role: Campaign analyst trained in graph uncertainty and privacy-preserving investigation
reviewer_path.escalation_role: Accountable trust-and-safety lead with legal/privacy consultation for cross-account action
evidence_requirements: Preserve edge definitions, confidence, time window, independent indicators, alternative explanations, account provenance, and campaign-level and account-level evidence.
reviewer_path.appeal_route: Each affected actor can challenge their linkage; an independent reviewer tests alternative explanations and can sever unsupported graph edges.

limitations: Graph methods amplify bad identifiers and can create guilt by association; campaign confidence must not erase individual review.
unresolved_questions: How can coordination evidence be shared or appealed without disclosing other users' private data?

sources.title: Threat Report on the Surveillance-for-Hire Industry
sources.claim_supported: Meta describes coordinated multi-stage activity across reconnaissance, engagement, and exploitation and reports network-level investigation and enforcement.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, Digital Services Act
sources.claim_supported: The DSA requires certain platforms to assess systemic risks while also providing statements of reasons and complaint mechanisms, illustrating the need to pair aggregate controls with individual recourse.

human_review: Route consequential findings to a reviewer with domain expertise, authority, and access only to the minimum necessary evidence.
Show the original evidence, detector/model/policy versions, timing, provenance, uncertainty, alternative explanations, and authorized-use twin.
Separate detection from adjudication. A model, score, graph edge, or rule hit is not a final finding.
Use additional specialist review for CBRN, employment, legal, cross-account, or high-impact account actions.
appeals: Provide notice and a useful reason unless doing so would create a documented safety, security, or legal risk.
Keep an appeal path available outside a suspected compromised session and assign a reviewer not responsible for the initial decision when feasible.
Allow correction of identity, authorization, role, accessibility, language, and campaign-linkage errors; record the evidence and reasons for reversal, narrowing, or affirmation.
Restore access or other state when appropriate, propagate corrections to dependent findings, and retain an auditable but proportionate record.
false_positives: Measure error rates by domain, timing, detector version, language, accessibility context, account segment, and reviewer outcome rather than one aggregate precision number.
Use abstention or queued review when evidence is insufficient, and avoid irreversible online action based only on content similarity or behavioral anomaly.
Sample negatives and successful appeals to find silent bias, missing authorized-use context, and correlated detector failures.
Treat absence of an appeal as weak evidence because affected people may lack notice, access, time, or trust.

global_limitations: These are research hypotheses for analyzers and review workflows, not enforcement policy or legal advice.
Most signals are dual use and context dependent. Authorized-use twins are expected, not exceptional.
Online decisions have the least context and highest urgency; nearline and offline review can reduce uncertainty but cannot recover evidence that was never retained.
Cross-service identity and campaign analysis can create privacy, sovereignty, and discrimination risks.
Attackers adapt to published controls, while reviewers and detectors can be deceived by poisoned context or prompt injection.
No system can provide perfect safety. Testament does not automatically enforce decisions.
